chartMethod: Phase 2 paints ChartKit and the libraries already timed on the line sweep: uPlot, Chart.js, ECharts, Recharts, Nivo, and Observable Plot. One cell per gallery type from apps/web/src/data/chart-types.ts. There is no type id area. The homepage row area is native stacked-area (full size, four series). A single filled line stays type line with mark.area true. mini-area is one filled series with the axes off, in the same 640×360 frame. Line cells are projected from the existing line sweep and are not measured again. Every other native cell uses the same point count as the ChartKit cell for that type, and the same data shape. The timer matches the line sweep: build data before the clock, paint, then wait for two animation frames. ECharts also waits for finished. The reported time is the median of BENCH_SAMPLES fresh pages (default 5) at 640×360. ChartKit updates are a second full paint. Marks stay SVG, except a dense scatter, a large heatmap, a long mini-area, and a long candlestick, which use ChartKit's canvas painter (axes stay SVG) because one node per mark, or a path with a command per pixel, cannot paint that N. The timer still waits for two animation frames after that paint. An error SVG (ck-chart-error) fails the sample. A cell is status unsupported, with a reason and no invented time, when that library has no native chart of that shape. Stand-ins are not timed: a pie made from bars, a waterfall made from a transparent helper bar, a histogram made from bars we binned ourselves, a sparkline made by hiding the axes on the line cell, a spike drawn as a bar, Plot.spike (a fixed-pixel vector), the uPlot candlestick demo path, an ECharts custom series, or the ECharts timeline playback control. Nivo cells use the 0.99.0 package for that chart, the same version as the pinned line, bar, and pie. A missing license key is status blocked. gzipBytes and ssrMs stay null until a later phase. Phase 3 adds the rest of the compare matrix and times the eleven gallery types that had no Phase-2 rival ok cell: bar-list, gantt, journey, kpi, progress-ring, quadrant, sparkline, spike, timeline, venn, and waterfall. ChartKit is painted again for those eleven, and for candlestick, so the comparison matches the canvas candlestick painter. Phase-2 rivals stay unsupported on the eleven and are not repainted. BENCH_PHASE=3 skips the line sweep. Candlestick is the extra type: Phase 2 had only ECharts, and a Phase-3 library is timed only when it has a native OHLC series.
